title: introduce-contractual-elasticity-advisor-and-burst-safeguard
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Adds a new advisory layer that enforces contractual elasticity targets and a burst-safeguard path; enables opt-in telemetry for percentiles and burst reconciliations; no public API breaking changes.
description: Motivation: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput guarantees that map to contractual SLAs while preserving the ability to safely accept short microbursts. This PR introduces the Contractual Elasticity Advisor (CEA): a control-plane advisory that computes target scale actions based on per-tenant commitments, multi-window utilization signals, and an explicit burst-safeguard budget that can be consumed without violating long-term guarantees. Design summary: CEA runs as a periodic evaluator (default 30s) and emits recommended scale intents with a confidence score. The serving reconciler consumes intents and applies a two-stage policy: 1) fast-path transient scale for burst budgets (ephemeral, bounded by burst tokens and short TTL), 2) sustained provision driven by contractual targets and smoothed utilization estimates. To avoid oscillation, we introduce a capped ramp limiter and probabilistic hysteresis that factors recent rollouts and active fallbacks. Telemetry: new time-series metrics (cea.intent_confidence, cea.recommended_delta, cea.burst_budget_consumed, cea.windowed_util_p95) and an event stream for intent->action transitions. Rollout plan: feature gated (config flag: enable_cea) and staged rollout to 10% of Dedicated clusters for 72 hours, with automated rollback if p99 latency or error rate increases by >5% relative. Backfill behavior: when burst budget is exhausted, requests are routed to compatible fallback model variants (lower-cost quantized variants) according to the tenant's fallback policy. Safety: added guarded path that pauses any scale-down that would drop committed throughput below the contract margin. Related work: follows ideas in ENG-4021 (throughput guarantees) and reuses telemetry conventions from ENG-4176. Testing and validation: unit/integration tests added, added e2e canary to perf-canary harness. Migration: default off; telemetry namespaced under cea.*; runbook updated for SRE and customer success.

Initial advisor evaluation loop and intent proto

- wire periodic job
- tests for evaluation window

Burst budget accounting and consumption path

- enforce TTL for transient allocations

Serving reconciler integration
- apply recommended intents to provisioner
- add safety checks to prevent contractual violation

Telemetry and dashboards
- add cea.* metrics and event trace
- dashboard JSON and alert rules

Docs and rollout config

review_comments: Ethan Cho: Overall this looks good. Question: how do we ensure the ephemeral burst allocations don't cause hot pod churn? Suggest adding a soft-min window before making another transient scale for the same tenant.
Priya Raman (author): Added probabilistic hysteresis and a two-minute soft-min per-tenant. See reconciler_integration.go:applyIntent for implementation.
Marina Vassilev: Can we expose an opt-out for customers that use third-party autoscaling? Also add a feature flag at cluster level.
Priya Raman (author): Added cluster-level feature flag enable_cea and tenant-level override; documented in docs/runbooks/cea-rollout.md.
Diego Alvarez: Telemetry looks solid; request adding a p99 of burst allocation latency to the dashboard.
Priya Raman (author): Added cea.burst_alloc_latency_p99 and updated dashboards/cea-summary.json.
Marina Vassilev: CI flake on integration test; reran and green.
Reviewer: approved (Ethan Cho), ready to merge after squash

monitoring: add alert cea.intent_confidence_drop (warn) and cea.burst_budget_drain (critical)
